story: Operator configures request-success and completion-latency objectives, inspects actual ingress arithmetic and burn state, and never receives a compliance claim from low traffic or incomplete/restarted collection.
browser: Actual connected Chrome creates and edits both policies through ordinary console forms. Both use real five-minute windows and minimum 50 observations. Success targets 99%; latency targets 95% within 250 ms; burn threshold 2.

An independent managed-ingress HTTP ledger contains 45 fast200s,3 interleaved 503s and2 slow 200s. Native SQLite records 50 completed requests, 47 successful and 48 completed within 250 ms; fast outer durations stay below 70 ms and slow outer durations exceed 321 ms.
At 5/5 complete minutes the browser shows success50/47/3, allowed0.5, remaining-2.5, burn6 and an open retained alert. Latency shows 50/48/2, allowed2.5, remaining0.5 and burn0.8 within budget.

Actual same-parent controller close/open changes collector epoch, retains exact version2 policies and the known 50-request bucket unchanged. The following4/5 window renders unavailable budget/burn and unknown retained alert, not recovery.
After the gap leaves the rolling window,5/5 complete minutes with 0 requests still render insufficient data and unavailable budget/burn; the alert remains unknown.

requirements.rollingWindows: Real wall/monotonic clocks and completed five-minute windows; no fabricated time or metric-row writes.
requirements.lowTraffic: Actual complete five-minute zero-request window remains insufficient.
requirements.missingBucketsAndRestart: Actual restart creates incomplete coverage, preserves the known bucket and marks retained burn unknown; native cases separately cover missed/overlapping collectors, clock reversal and missing buckets.

nativeRequirementCases: sole persistent SLO collector seals known-zero minutes and records real terminal fractions
restart, overlapping collectors, missed heartbeats and wall-clock reversal cannot certify a window
actual native ingress completion, server failure and cancelled body reach the SLO histogram
two real SQLite policy controllers preserve one exact creation and one accepted stale-version contender
native SLO policies retain exact actor receipts and current versions across restart
SLO viewers can inspect coverage while writes require a current explicit project grant
native SLO body intake revalidates exact tokens, membership, session, permission and storage protocol
missing, partial, empty and low-traffic minutes never establish compliance or resolve a burn
qualifications: Focused 78 combines native API/SQLite/ingress cases and client/console/evaluation contracts; actual Chrome and real-clock HTTP evidence is separate. No physical authenticator or production host certification is claimed.

The initial planned run tripped the existing circuit breaker after consecutive503s. The interleaved run completed all 50 HTTP status/body checks, then its stale scheduled-minute assertion failed. Acceptance uses independently retained actual request timestamps, native histogram and browser full-window values; both unsuccessful harness records remain preserved. No production assertion, timeout, policy safeguard, metric value or clock was weakened.
Controller reopen is same-parent close/open. Known counts are compared before/after that actual restart; later normal rolling-window expiry is not data loss.
